newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse returns to upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse returns to upward trend.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange on Thursday ended the session 0.24 percent higher after three consecutive days of decline, a broker said.
The rise was due largely to trading in Financiere Diwan, he said.
Diwan, a subsidiary of Morocco's largest private ONA Group, rose 25 dirhams to close at 235 dirhams.
The firm has a market capitalisation of nearly 2.0 billion dirhams, a trader said.

Analysts at Upline Securities said the rise in the Diwan closing price "implicates a hike in the financial sub-index which increased from 405.77 points to 409.20 points gaining 0.85 percent over the previous session."
The all-share index closed at 433.73 points, up from 432.68 points on Wednesday,.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the country's second largest private conglomerate, lost two dirhams to close at 552 dirhams.
Samir oil firm, Morocco's main refinery, remained unchanged at 250 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market largest capitalisation was stable at 688 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 23 million dirhams against 22.5 million on Wednesday, officials said.
